LESSON: WRITING 2.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can we become better at spelling? 2. How does spelling affect written communication?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. search online or offline for examples of abbreviations, acronyms, frequently misspelt and easily confused words. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. search online or offline for examples of abbreviations, acronyms, frequently misspelt and easily confused words. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 2.4.1 Mechanics of Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy - self-awareness as the learner sorts out their priorities as they search online or offline for examples of

abbreviations.

● Communication and collaboration - writing clearly as learner advances the skill of spelling while designing charts and

posters featuring abbreviations, acronyms, words with affixes, frequently misspelt and easily confused words.

Values:
36

● Responsibility - diligence is enhanced as the learner diligently uses the internet while searching for abbreviations and

frequently confused words.

● Patriotism is promoted as the learner respects classmates as they design charts and posters featuring abbreviations,

acronyms, words with affixes, frequently misspelt and easily confused words and display them.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Socio-economic issues - Climate change: The learner brings out issues on climate change in self-written paragraphs.

Suggested Learning Resources: Locally available materials to make customised cultural objects, language games, digital

resources, authentic texts, internet, dictionaries and thesauruses adapted digital devices with filter keys/key guards/larger

mouse/head control input devices such as head wand. universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips
